correctness.rationale: The pointwise log-coordinate and linear combination identities hold symbolically for arbitrary positive rate constants. Invariance gives zero expected generator of every smooth test function; compact interior support legitimizes log tests. The exact x defect is a nonnegative weighted square and the y excess a strictly positive variance except on the equilibrium. Zero defect implies that the complete invariant support is the unique equilibrium by direct restriction of the vector field. Standalone symbolic replay succeeds.

originality.rationale: The central 2022 primary full-text Section 5 proves Hopf existence and the equilibrium but not the conditional generator identities or the strict, opposite pair of mean defects. The original Wilhelm 2009 paper centers on a distinct two-species bistable system, with mention of the oscillator and no inspected equivalent stationary moment theorem. Semantic index searches for the exact three-species ODE, source aliases, and conditional means returned only different chemical systems. Generic stationarity-generator calculus is recognized as the method but does not give these concrete rate-dependent strict signs without the three displayed model-specific polynomial identities. Unindexed coincident derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: No global novelty guarantee: an unindexed earlier derivation using standard generator identities could exist.
The full text of each unrelated indexed stationary-moment paper was not needed for model identity but was not read, so no whole-document noncoverage judgment is made.
The three-reaction related survey was assessed at abstract/bibliographic level only.
The result is deterministic and conditional on compact interior invariant support, not a blanket statement about every positive trajectory.

value.rationale: In a published minimal four-reaction biochemical oscillator with actual stable periodic solutions, exact physical-time concentration statistics reveal a universal, sharp polarity: mean X lies below its unique equilibrium, mean Y above, and mean Z equals its equilibrium; conditional catalytic mean is fixed on every Y fiber. This answers the natural equilibrium-versus-oscillation yield question for all positive rates and all compact positive invariant states, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Defects measure the effect quantitatively and vanish exactly on equilibrium.
